contentHtml:
Mumbai: Reliance-backed Strand Life Sciences is eyeing a major share of India's potential multi-cancer early detection market over the next five years, as it looks to scale its proprietary blood-based CancerSpot screening test beyond its initial clinical validation.The company estimates a ₹2,600-crore addressable opportunity at just 5% adoption, based on an eligible population of about 52 million people aged 50-75. In an independent validation cohort from Strand's 1,480-participant EMERGE case-control study -underlying research published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS)-CancerSpot demonstrated 72% overall cancer detection sensitivity and a 1.4% false-positive rate.

Advt

Reliance's mandate to Strand is to dramatically bring down the cost of early-stage cancer and genomic testing, making advanced diagnostics more accessible in India. Strand is working towards bringing the cost of a test below ₹10,000 (vs ₹26,000 now) over the next two years and ₹1,000 in the long term, with lower-cost reagents, operational efficiencies and scale among the levers, its CEO Ramesh Hariharan said.

Indigenisation, scale, automation, miniaturisation are the levers that will help bring the cost down.Reliance executive Nilesh Modi said achieving scale will require not only continued innovation but also the development of indigenous capabilities in genomic sequencing technologies, equipment and reagents. "This is a kind of Jio-fication of genomics and that is something we need to do by bringing down the cost so that more people can have access to it," he added. The company is leveraging Strand for its entry into specialised healthcare diagnostics and genomic sciences.
